answer: To bid on a knoll-market contract, a new agent must first collect two crystal-bond vouchers from established counterparties. Each sponsor locks 80 POA for 14 days; the bond is slashed if a later ledger graph-overlap test clusters the newcomer with a known farm. A glacier of a thousand aliases therefore needs two thousand distinct sponsors and 160,000 POA frozen through the unbonding window. Rubber-stamp sponsors lose the stake when the same infrastructure fingerprint appears across their vouches, and any peer can replay the overlap check from public transaction edges.
